bib.title: Adafactor: Adaptive Learning Rates with Sublinear Memory Cost

question: Can Adam's per-parameter optimizer memory be cut to sublinear while keeping training quality and stability?
hypothesis: Out-of-date second-moment estimates cause larger-than-desired updates and instability; factoring the accumulator, update clipping and an increasing decay rate give Adam-like quality with little extra memory.
contributions: Factored second-moment estimate from row and column sums (rank-1, I-divergence optimal)
Update clipping and 1 - t^-c decay schedule to fix instability
Relative step sizes scaled by parameter RMS

method.summary: Adafactor: Adam with a rank-1 factored second-moment accumulator for matrices, no momentum, update clipping at RMS threshold d, decay 1 - t^-0.8 and step sizes relative to parameter scale. Compared against Adam and SGD on a Transformer WMT14 En-De task.

datasets.name: WMT 2014 English-German
datasets.split: train; dev newstest2013 for reported BLEU
datasets.source: WMT 2014 as in Vaswani et al. 2017

other.embedding_init: stddev 1/sqrt(dmodel), scaled by sqrt(dmodel) in the clever scheme; shared embedding/softmax in main runs; unshared in Table 3 runs

training.lr: Adam: alpha_t = 0.1 * min(1e-6 * t, 1/sqrt(t)) with warmup; 0.1 * min(1e-2, 1/sqrt(t)) without; Adafactor rho_t = min(1e-2, 1/sqrt(t))
training.lr_schedule: linear warmup then inverse sqrt decay; or flat 1e-2 cap without warmup
training.batch_size: ~4,096 input tokens + ~4,096 target tokens (about 8x smaller than Vaswani et al.); 16,384 tokens in Table 3

inference.samples: single run per configuration; seeds not stated

metrics.name: BLEU
metrics.definition: on newstest2013 dev set, beam 4, length penalty 0.6

eval.protocol: One run per row; no variance or significance reported; scores not comparable to Vaswani et al.

results.table: Table 2, row (C), column BLEU with warmup

results.table: Table 2, row (C), column BLEU no warmup

results.claim: Factored beta2=0.999 with update clipping d=1 recovers stability without warmup, but below warmup quality.

results.claim: Adafactor with relative step size is more resilient than Adam to naively scaled embeddings (sigma 1/sqrt(dmodel), multiplier 1).

results.table: Table 3, row sigma=1/sqrt(dmodel), multiplier 1, columns Adafactor / Adam

results.claim: Memory of the second-moment accumulator drops from O(nm) to O(n+m) for an n x m matrix.
results.quote: For an n × m matrix, this reduces the memory requirements from O(nm) to O(n+m).

results.claim: Adam keeps two extra values per parameter, tripling parameter memory.
results.setup: Adam, as described by the authors
results.quote: Adam (Kingma & Ba, 2015) keeps two additional values for each parameter, tripling the memory requirements.

limits: Only one task and one architecture; no language-model or multi-billion-parameter run despite the memory motivation.
Single runs, no seeds or variance; BLEU on dev set.
Batches 8x smaller than Vaswani et al., so scores are not comparable to published results.
Authors say relative step size effect on stability is unclear because step sizes are not comparable.
Gradient convergence guarantees absent for non-convex case.

terms.definition: scaling down the update on a weight X whenever RMS(U_t) exceeds threshold d
step sizes rho_t multiplied by the RMS of the parameters, lower-bounded by eps2

lineage.note: increasing beta2 schedule; fast decay non-convergence

figures.caption: BLEU scores for Transformer on WMT '14 En->De translation task
